title: LTS release contract and deployment gates playbook
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Create a pragmatic, implementable LTS release contract that ties together versioning semantics, cross-surface support windows (runtime, API, SDKs, Console), automated preflight checks, and deployment gates. The playbook should enable predictable upgrades for customers on LTS lanes, reduce rollback surface, and define automation hooks for canary -> ramp -> cohort stages. Deliverables: a support matrix artifact, gating criteria (metrics + tests), automation checklist for upgrade-orchestrator jobs, and a set of preflight validators in CI.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical support matrix (CSV/JSON) that lists minimum compatible runtime, API, SDK, console versions per LTS band
A documented release contract paragraph suitable for public docs and customer SLA pages
Automated preflight validators run in CI and block releases on failures (compatibility tests, e2e smoke, perf smoke)
Deployment gates codified in the upgrade orchestrator: canary pass, latency/regression thresholds, error-rate limits, cost-per-token regression limits
Rollback choreography documented and runnable via playbook scripts with a one-button abort for active rollouts
Console UI contains visible rollout state and per-route model/version pins for customers in affected cohorts
decisions: Adopt semantic-banding: major.minor.patch where 'LTS band' = even minor numbers with 12-month guaranteed security + critical fixes
Backwards-compatible API changes allowed within minor; breaking changes require major bump + explicit migration guide
Runtime will guarantee request/response schema compatibility for N minor increments (N = 2) with automated contract tests
SDKs will provide adapters for two LTS bands; console will surface deprecation warnings 90 days before enforcement
Rollout gates to include: canary success (30% traffic for 2h), latency P95 regression < 2x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.5 percentage points, token cost delta < 5%
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting with release-ops, runtime, SDK and console leads. Agreed on scope and deliverables.

2026-03-03: Spike completed for automated compatibility fingerprint tool (proto on GH: github.com/redwood/inference/compat-fingerprint/pull/12). Early results show 93% coverage for core API contracts.
2026-03-06: Perf gating thresholds drafted after running synthetic workloads against runtime-2.3. Noted 1-2% baseline variance; will set guard rails conservatively.
2026-03-09: Design review with PM and Legal on public-facing contract language. Legal requested explicit SLA language for security patches in LTS bands.
2026-03-12: Integration tests flaked in CI on macOS runners (time-sensitive KV cache warmup). Filed ENG-325010 to stabilize tests; temporarily disabled non-blocking tests in preflight.
2026-03-14: Draft playbook ready in Confluence for internal review; pulling in feedback from infra and customer success. Preparing final PR for automation changes.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: tighter gating reduces customer exposure but increases release latency. We prioritized customer uptime for LTS customers (longer canary + stricter error thresholds) and faster rollbacks. We will revisit minor-band cadence after two LTS cycles. Security review is required before any public SLA changes. Follow-up: schedule tabletop runbook drill with SRE and Customer Success (assigned to Diego).
